title: Proposal for Permanent Baby Gift to Support New Parents
what_it_is: Proposal for Permanent Baby Gift to Support New Parents

sections.label: Permanent baby gift proposal
sections.summary: The Ministry has no plans to introduce baby gifts permanently, as such gifts mark national milestones.

sentences.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee
sentences.text: asked the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance whether the Ministry will consider permanently introducing a baby gift, similar to Singapore's SG60 Baby Gift and Finland's baby box scheme, to support new parents with parenting essentials.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: There are currently no plans to introduce such gifts on a permanent basis as the purpose of these gifts is to mark special milestones in our nation's journey.

sections.label: Baby Bonus and Large Families Scheme
sections.summary: Parents can use the Baby Bonus Cash Gift for baby essentials, and the Large Families Scheme gives credits for third and subsequent children.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: For instance, parents have flexibility in using the Baby Bonus Cash Gift, which ranges from $11,000 for the first and second child, to $13,000 for the third and subsequent children, to purchase baby essentials.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: We have also introduced the Large Families Scheme, under which parents with three or more children will receive $1,000 of Large Family LifeSG Credits each year for every third and subsequent Singapore Citizen child, from the year that the child turns one to the year that the child turns six.

sections.label: Cash support for parents
sections.summary: The Baby Bonus Cash Gift and First Step Grant give cash to parents, who choose what they need.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: It is meant to be something to mark a milestone.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But in terms of the essentials and what is needed, what most parents actually need is the cash.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And hence, that is why we have the Baby Bonus Cash Gift.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And also, why we have the First Step Grant, which puts cash into the hands of the parents and then, they can choose what they want.

sections.label: No survey on Baby Gift
sections.summary: The Minister is not aware of any survey on the Baby Gift, which was not intended as a policy measure.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: As to whether any survey or study was done on the impact of the Baby Gift, not that I am aware of.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: I may stand corrected, but not that I am aware of, simply because the Baby Gift was not intended to be a policy measure to achieve a certain outcome.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: It was just intended to be a nice thing to commemorate a special occasion.
